direction: E7: Solver sensitivity. For which solver do text skills matter? (glm-5.3-flash vs glm-5.3 vs deepseek-v4-flash with thinking off, plus a JSON-format diagnostic)
refuted_claims:
1. CLAIM: "可见 v3 在 SearchQA 上'规则通不过'，很大程度是格式造成的" / "the deepseek-v4-flash thinking-off 'rules don't help' result on SearchQA is substantially a format artifact".
   - CHECKED: answer-tag share and JSON replies in every v3 train/screen/confirm cell, stages 1-3, both chains. Read-only, no evaluation dirs. Script: /data/feasibility/E7-critic/v3_tagshare_all.py on the new machine.
   - FOUND, primary chain I-ds: in the s1 SearchQA screen, the parent and all 3 screened rules (s1-r1, s1-r2, s1-r4) have tag share 1.000 and 0 JSON replies. I-ds s3 is ≥0.93 with 0 JSON.
   - FOUND, where drift exists: only in E-ds s1. s1-r1 (= cal-1 cand) is 0.694 in screen and 0.784 in confirm, with 44 and 43 JSON replies; s1-r3 is 0.891 with 20.
   - For s1-r1 the claim holds strongly. I re-scored the real v3 cells JSON-aware (/data/feasibility/E7-critic/eds_s1_json.py): screen goes from +0.75 to +13.75 items of 200, confirm from -2.50 to +12.25.
   - So the artifact explains the secondary chain's single best rule (which restates the task card), not the primary chain's null. At most 1-2 of the 7 screened SearchQA rules are affected.

2. CLAIM: "Untagged replies are mostly JSON".
   - CHECKED: all 8,800 cal-1 cells.
   - FOUND: JSON makes up 118 of 311 untagged cand replies (38%), 21 of 189 for seed-rule (11%), 76 of 276 for seed-rule3, and about 30% overall.
   - 47% of untagged cand replies pass through the last-line fallback. JSON is the failing subset, not the majority.

3. CLAIM: the remedy "put the answer contract last (historical layout)".
   - CHECKED: docs/handoff/coevo5-pipeline-audit-20261019.md §4.1.
   - FOUND: under the historical layout, deepseek tagged only 21 of 100 OfficeQA training replies (v2 smoke), and a gate parent 10 of 54. Contract-first was introduced as the fix for this.
   - Reverting reopens the defect on OfficeQA and LiveMath, whose scorers require the tag and have no fallback. A JSON-aware extraction, or stating the contract at both ends, is safe.

4. CLAIM: "要检测一条规则这么大的效果，大约 50 道题就够", used as the case for flash.
   - That number is power against the EMPTY scaffold.
   - CHECKED: per-item sd of the owner's contrast (rule vs task card).
   - FOUND, flash: sd 0.168, so 80% power needs about 89 items for +5 pp and 247 for +3 pp; the minimum detectable effect at 200 items is 3.3 pp.
   - FOUND, format-fixed deepseek: sd 0.243, about 186 and 515 items; minimum detectable effect 4.8 pp.
   - Flash is the quieter instrument for this contrast (the explorer missed this), but +3 pp is still beyond a 200-item stage pool.

5. CLAIM: flash is the best purpose-2 instrument.
   - CHECKED: the same records rescored with sub_em (gold contained in the answer, or the reverse).
   - FOUND: on flash, ids-full and cand move -3.6 pp [-7.7, 0.0] and -2.6 pp; on glm-5.3 and deepseek about 0. The gains exist only under strict exact match (and F1 about +7).
   - So every measured SearchQA skill effect is answer surface form, such as stripping parentheticals. Nothing suggests it would carry over to OfficeQA numbers or LiveMath option letters.
   - Picking the solver on which this effect is largest is instrument selection driven by the outcome.

6. CLAIM: SkillsBench shows "最强的模型提高最多".
   - CHECKED: v1 Table 3.
   - FOUND: the largest gain is Claude Opus 4.5 (+23.3 pp), but the best configuration with Skills is Gemini 3 Flash (48.7% vs 45.3%). Opus 4.6 gained among the least (+13.9). The paper states no strength rule.
   - The "7 configurations, +13.6 to +23.3 pp" figures are correct for v1 only. v4 has 18 configurations (+4.1 to +25.7 pp), and the NeurIPS 2026 version reports 18 of 84 tasks regressing.

7. Minor errors.
   - "fewest flips with guidance": under ids-full, deepseek flips least (3.1% vs flash 5.1%).
   - "tail cell 193 s / 14,011 completion tokens": the largest flash SearchQA cell used 31,956 of 32,768 tokens and took 444 s (ids-full); 4 of 686 cells exceed 8K tokens.
   - "flash placebo about 0": rests on 1 placebo x 1 run. control:2, the placebo that still gives +3.6 pp on deepseek, was not run.

8. CLAIM: "about 30M tokens, comparable to cal-1 (27.5M)".
   - This compares an estimate of receipt usage with a ledger figure.
   - FOUND: cal-1's own receipts sum to 14.0M (17.6M charged), but its ledger settled 27.5M.
   - A registered cal-1-flash at about 15M receipt usage implies roughly 25-30M ledger tokens. Caps must allow for that; cal-1 paused on its cap for exactly this reason.
confirmed_claims:
- PILOT NUMBERS: recomputed independently from raw records (my own script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dulin-Documents-Paper-SkillOpt/e7258b97-b430-4dd5-959d-eb871e7c777f/scratchpad/feas/E7-critic/verify1.py). Pass rates, paired means, bootstrap CIs, up/down counts, sign p, flips and tag shares all match.
  - deepseek: ids-full +0.102 [0.036, 0.173] 19/4; cand -0.046 13/17; control:3 -0.092 7/21; parent:B 0.000 8/8.
  - flash: ids-full +0.143 22/1; cand +0.138 21/2; control:3 -0.005 8/8; cand minus ids-full -0.005 4/4.
  - glm-5.3: ids-full +0.092 14/1; cand +0.061 14/7, p=0.19.
- INTEGRITY:
  - 1,300 of 1,300 GLM requests are byte-identical to cal-1 (request hash).
  - Returned model ids are correct.
  - flash reasoned in 588 of 588 answered cells; glm-5.3 in only 79 of 588, with mean completion 15-17 tokens, so it is effectively non-thinking.
  - The 2 excluded items are BigModel 1301 refusals in every arm and run.
- cal-1: the registered A3/A5 numbers reproduce exactly from the compact export (ids-full +0.0938 48/13/139; cand -0.0262 37/44; control:3 -0.0975 16/58; control:2 +0.0362).
- SCORER: evaluator.extract_answer's last-line fallback turns '{"answer": "U2"}' into 'answer u2', which fails exact match.
- JSON-AWARE DIAGNOSTIC:
  - My independent re-score on the pilot items reproduces cand +0.071 [0.010, 0.133] 15/5 p=0.041 and control:3 -0.010.
  - The 200x4 arithmetic checks: cand +0.0675, control:3 -0.0025, cand minus ids-full -0.010, control:2 still +0.036.
  - So cal-1's "placebo shifts -9.8 pp" is mostly a format effect, but the +3.6 pp placebo is not. This correction matters for D5 and D8.
- v3 E-ds s1-r1 really is damaged by format drift. JSON-aware it would net +12 to +14 items in both screen and confirm, so its C2 failure (-15/2) is plausibly an artifact.
- LITERATURE:
  - SkillsBench v1 numbers are right, and a NeurIPS 2026 poster exists.
  - Dynamic Cheatsheet: limited gains for GPT-4o-mini and "minimal or inconsistent" gains for R1/o1, confirmed.
  - The DeepSeek-R1 sentence "sensitive to prompts. Few-shot prompting consistently degrades its performance" is verbatim (lines 732-735 of the local copy). But it concerns R1 and few-shot prompting, so it only indirectly supports claims about deepseek-v4-flash with thinking off.
- LEDGER CONSISTENCY: the in-family bias on generated items and "learned minus bzero is null on real items across 3 models" match the 10/16 00:50 ledger entry.
- COST: E7's spend of 2,869,652 tokens checks arithmetically.
- "No solver shows learned > good instruction" is consistent with the data, though it was only tested as the rule alone vs the card.
missing:
- The owner's actual I-ds contrast, task card + learned rule vs task card, was not run on any solver. The conclusion is inferred from the rule alone vs the card.
- The explorer did not re-analyse the v3 gate cells before claiming a v3-wide artifact. Done here: only E-ds s1 is affected.
- No lenient-metric check. sub_em shows every effect is answer surface form under strict exact match.
- No baseline plan or cost for a solver switch.
  - The v3 delta says SkillOpt and GEPA exist only on GLM-5.3 and become non-comparable once the solver changes.
  - The original registration estimated about 170M tokens for those two baselines.
- No discussion of the registered "weaker student, stronger teacher" premise. Per the 10/16 ledger, flash with a Skill outscored GLM-5.3 on OfficeQA.
- Nothing on the verifier side (purpose 1, the coding rubric).
  - The flash recommendation forces a ban on generated panels as transfer evidence. That is the co-evolution pathway the owner wants to run every step.
  - No alternative is offered, such as a generator or judge from another model family.
- The OfficeQA transfer probe is underspecified and underpowered.
  - It does not say which section the SearchQA rule goes in. A rule under the SearchQA "Applies when" header is inert on OfficeQA by design.
  - 74 items x 2 runs gives a minimum detectable effect around 10 pp by the explorer's own numbers, so it is likely uninformative at about 10M tokens and 4-5 h.
- Only 1 placebo was run on flash, and none on glm-5.3.
- Any scorer change must be applied to every arm and baseline, and it departs from comparability with native SearchQA exact match.
- The owner's "刷分" lever is the choice of benchmark, not the choice of solver.
- Verification scripts:

  - New machine: /data/feasibility/E7-critic/{v3_tagshare.py, v3_tagshare_all.py, eds_s1_json.py}
notes_cn:
一句话：E7 的实验做得扎实，我从原始记录重算，数字全部对得上。但它的两个主要结论要打折扣。它真正有用的只有一件不花钱的事：让评分器也认 JSON 格式的答案（JSON 是一种数据格式）。这件事已经在 v4 的修复清单里。

一、“格式问题”只影响次要的那条链。
- E7 说，v3 在 SearchQA（检索问答）上规则通不过，很大程度是格式造成的。
- 我直接查了 v3 第 1 到 3 步的门槛记录。门槛就是接受规则前的检验；我只读了训练题。
- 主链 I-ds（从写好的任务说明出发，也就是您最关心的“学到的规则能不能胜过好说明”）：父 Skill 和三条被检验的规则，100% 都把答案写在要求的标签里，一条 JSON 回答都没有。格式问题在主链上不存在。
- 只有次要链 E-ds（从空架子出发）第 1 步的那条规则受影响，也就是 cal-1（校准实验）里的 cand。按 JSON 也算的话：
  - 初筛：从多 0.75 题变成多 13.75 题（共 200 题）；
  - 复核：从少 2.5 题变成多 12.25 题。
  所以它当初在复核时被判“伤了其余题”，很可能是格式造成的。修好评分器，它大概率会被收下。但这条规则的内容本来就是任务说明里已有的话。所以修评分器能让次要链“从零学回任务说明”，不会改变“学到的规则胜不过好说明”这个主结论。
- 有一个新的、有用的更正：cal-1 里那段“菜谱”无关文字让分数掉 9.8 点，按 JSON 也算只掉 0.25 点。“无关文字会让分数大幅波动”这个说法主要是格式造成的。但“十六进制颜色”那段无关文字仍然多 3.6 点，格式解释不了。

二、E7 给的另一个修法不能用。它建议“把答案要求放回提示最后”（旧排法）。10/19 的审计已经发现，旧排法下 deepseek 在 OfficeQA（文档问答）上 100 个回答只有 21 个带标签，正是因此才改成现在的排法。稳妥的做法是：让评分器认 JSON 答案，或者把答案要求在提示开头和结尾各写一遍。

三、换成 glm-5.3-flash 做题，效果看起来更大，但全是“答案写法”。
- 换一种判法：只看答案里是否包含正确的名字，不要求一字不差。这样判，任务说明和学到的规则在 flash 上反而少 3.6 和 2.6 点，在三个模型上都约等于 0。
- 也就是说，提升全部来自把答案写得和标准答案一模一样（例如去掉括号说明），模型找对答案的次数并没有变多。
- 这种写法规则是 SearchQA 特有的，没有理由迁移到 OfficeQA 的数字答案或 LiveMath（选择题数学）的选项。
- 按“谁效果最大就选谁”挑做题模型，审稿人会认为是在挑测量工具。

四、“约 50 道题就够”是规则对比空架子时的数字。您的标准是规则对比好说明：
- flash 上，要看出 5 点提升约需 90 道题，3 点约需 250 道；
- 修好格式的 deepseek 上，分别约需 190 道和 520 道。
flash 在这个对比上噪声确实小约三分之一，这是 E7 没提到的优点。但 3 点左右的提升，200 道的训练池仍然看不出来。E7 也没有在任何模型上真正跑“说明加规则”对比“说明”。

五、与您两个核心目的的关系。
- 协同进化（Skill 和验证端的评分细则一起进化）：E7 完全没涉及验证端。而且做题模型换成 GLM 家族后，出题和判题也是 GLM，生成题上的结果会偏向同一家族。E7 自己也只好规定生成题不能当迁移证据，这等于放弃了“每步生成新题”这条路。
- 在一个 bench 上进化、在其余 bench 上评测：E7 没测任何迁移。它提议的 OfficeQA 迁移实验只有 74 道题，按它自己算的灵敏度只能看出 10 点左右的差别；也没说规则放在哪个分区。大概率测不出东西，却要约 1000 万 token（token 是计费的字数单位）、4 到 5 小时。
- 隐藏成本有三项：
  - 对比方法 SkillOpt 和 GEPA 只在 GLM-5.3 上跑过，换模型就要全部重跑（原登记估计约 1.7 亿 token），E7 没算。
  - v3 选 deepseek 的理由是“做题的弱一点、当老师的强一点”。10/16 的记录显示，flash 加了说明后在 OfficeQA 上比 GLM-5.3 还强，这个前提就不成立了。
  - cal-1 的账本实际记了 2750 万 token，回答本身只用了 1400 万。E7 用回答本身的用量估 1500 万；正式登记的运行要按约两倍设上限，否则会像 cal-1 一样中途停。

六、文献核对。
- SkillsBench 的“7 个配置、提高 13.6 到 23.3 点”与第一版一致，但“最强的模型提高最多”不对：提高最多的 Claude Opus 4.5 并不是最强的配置，Opus 4.6 反而提高最少。会议版还报告 84 道题里有 18 道变差。
- Dynamic Cheatsheet 和 DeepSeek-R1 的引文属实。但 R1 那句话讲的是推理模型和带示例的提示，拿来解释 deepseek-v4-flash 不思考时的行为很勉强。

建议：
- 只做不花钱的部分：让评分器认 JSON 答案，作为新版本登记；重算 cal-1 和 v3 E-ds 第 1 步；把“每种文字下带标签的比例”作为常设检查。
- 暂不把 flash 作为主做题模型。如果要用，先补“说明加规则”对比“说明”这组对照，并拿出基线重跑和 GLM 家族偏差的方案。
